title_text: 12 Tips to Create a Safe and Comfortable Environment For Your Baby
content_text: Starting a family is one of the most exciting moments in a person’s life. It has been seen as an idea or dream for so long, and knowing that someone you love is finally with you, the moving day can not come soon enough. However, starting with a baby can be overwhelming if you don’t know what to expect. In order to make the transition as smooth as possible, here are some tips on creating a comfortable environment for your baby. 1. Clear Your Clutter There are many things to remember when you first become a parent. You will want to take note of things such as how much food the baby can eat and how much they should be sleeping at night. A clutter-free household can create a safe environment for your baby to explore while maintaining order in your home. It is important to keep your baby’s room as organized as possible. If there are items out of order, it can cause them to feel unsettled or unconfident. Having a clean and well-organized environment will train their senses, blocking out any unnecessary stimuli. 2. Choose Baby Items and Accessories In Moderation As a parent, you will want to buy everything you can think of to make your baby more comfortable. When shopping for items and accessories, it is important to remember that you don’t need to buy everything at once. You should only buy what your baby needs and avoid purchasing things such as extra clothes or toys unless they are needed. You also need to ensure that your baby can easily access the items you already have. The less confusion there is for them, the better chance of developing good habits and routines. 3. Set Aside a Space for Your Baby’s Sleep When trying to put your baby down for sleep, you will want to make sure that there is a clear space for them to fall asleep in. If there is not enough room for them to fall asleep comfortably, it can be frustrating and stressful. When your little one sleeps in the same room as you, it can be easier to wake them in the middle of the night and disrupt your rest. It is best to use a separate sleeping area to keep all noises to a minimum and distractions are gone. 4. Use Room Temperature to Create a Relaxing Temperature When choosing an infant’s sleep area, it is important to make sure that the temperature is not too hot or too cold. It can be overwhelming to try and fall asleep when the temperature is too high. Many parents choose to place thermostats in their infant’s sleeping area. You will want to choose a comfortable temperature that gives you enough time to turn out the lights and relax before your baby wakes up and disturbs you again. 5. Create A Clean and Safe Play Environment An ideal way to allow your baby to explore without worrying about possible injuries is by creating a safe play environment for them. It is a good idea to create an area where they can climb, crawl, jump and play safely. You should include mats or pads on the floor in case they fall, and make sure that no toys are too small for their mouths or could break into pieces that could cause choking hazards later on down the line. 6. Create A Positive Environment Your baby’s environment can be very important in their development and sense of security throughout their childhood and into adulthood. Nonverbal communication is very important to see how well they are adjusting. Make sure to give them plenty of cues that you are comfortable in their presence, including signing and offering your body language as well. 7. Schedule Breaks During the first months of your baby’s life, it is important to make sure that there are enough breaks from each day to prevent over-exposure and burnout. It can be hard for a new parent, especially an exhausted one, to get enough rest in order for their baby’s needs. Still, the both of you must have time to rest so that you can be just as energetic and excited as they are when they wake up in the morning. 8. Try to Make Your Baby’s Bedtime Pleasant It is another thing to consider when making your baby’s bedtime comfortable. For example, making sure that the area is dark enough and limiting their exposure to bright lights before bed may help them get ready for sleep faster. Giving them a bottle of water that they haven’t had allows them to associate it with sleep time and makes it easier for them to fall asleep on their own. 9. Eliminate All Light Sources When you first become a parent, it may seem like there is light everywhere that they are not supposed to be in. You may notice that there are all of these extra lights with your baby’s name on them or even lights along the side of their crib that are not necessary. You will want to eliminate these light sources as much as possible. You can cover them up with fabric or even purchase a special light-blocking film to completely block out any unwanted lights inside of your baby’s room. 10. Keep Hot Foods And Liquids Out Of Reach When you are a new parent, you spend most of your day around your baby. You will want to make sure that very few things could harm them, especially anywhere in their reach. You will want to keep any hot foods or liquids away from them, as well as any cleaning product since they could easily be consumed by mistake. 11. Limit Their Exposure To Germs When you are trying to keep the household clean, it is important to eliminate the potential for germs and bacteria. You can accomplish it by ensuring that no dirty dishes or utensils are ever left around the house and that no items are lying around with mold or dirt on them. 12. Be Careful Of Over Stimulation As a parent, you will want your child to be around as many people and things as possible so they can become comfortable with different environments and sounds. However, you will want to keep a watchful eye for overstimulation because this can cause anxiety and even nightmares. Over-stimulation is defined by excessive excitement or overstimulation to meet a child’s needs. These are a few things to keep in mind when you are a new parent. It is important to remember that everything will change as your child grows older and becomes more independent. You can figure out new routines that work for the both of you, and be sure that your baby feels safe and comfortable no matter where they are. __________________ I’m Andrea Gibbs Born, raised, and still living in New York. I’m a work-at-home mom with a background in business development, strategy, and social media marketing. I’m a blog contributor at Baby Steps Daycare in Rego Park, New York to motivate and educate other parents about how they can get their children ahead of the game in school.
